cards.title: Bias in Parameter Estimates from BQL Handling Methods
cards.claim: Omission of BQL data causes substantial bias in parameter estimates (e.g., absorption rate constant KA, mean transit time MTT, clearance CL, drug effect SLOP). Substitution with LOQ/2 yields unpredictable bias patterns, sometimes reducing and sometimes inflating bias compared to omission. The M3 method (likelihood-based) generally provides unbiased parameter estimates.
conditions: Applicable to nonlinear mixed-effects models (e.g., NONMEM).
Validated for BQL occurring in absorption phases, elimination phases, and indirect response PD models.
Bias magnitude increases with higher LOQ levels and higher percentages of BQL data.
required_inputs: Software capable of likelihood-based estimation (e.g., NONMEM VI with F_FLAG for M3).
limitations: M3 method requires longer runtimes and has a lower rate of successful minimization/covariance steps compared to FOCE.
Results are based on simulation studies; real-world applicability depends on correct structural model specification.
Laplacian estimation (required for M2/M3 in this study) had higher non-successful termination rates than FOCE.
cards.downstream_use: Select M3 (or equivalent likelihood-based censoring method) as the primary strategy for handling BQL data in population PK/PD modeling to minimize bias. Avoid simple omission or LOQ/2 substitution unless justified by specific constraints.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
